items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region (nonempty, bounded, open, [[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval ([[def-interval]]). A **motion of $B$ on $I$** consists of an open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ with $\overline B\subseteq O$ ([[def-metric-ball]]) together with a map $$\chi:I\times O\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3$$ such that: 1. $\chi$ is of class $C^2$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); 2. for every $t\in I$ the map $\chi_t:=\chi(t,\cdot):O\to\mathbb R^3$ is of class $C^1$, is injective, and has $D_X\chi_t(X)$ invertible for every $X\in O$; 3. writing $$J(t,X):=\det\bigl(D_X\chi_t(X)\bigr)$$ with the determinant of [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]], one has $J(t,X)>0$ for every $(t,X)\in I\times B$. We call $X\in B$ the **material label** (reference position), $x=\chi(t,X)$ the **position** at time $t$ of the label $X$, and $$\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$$ the **current (material) region** at time $t$. items.title: The derivative of the determinant along an invertible C¹ matrix curve: $(\det A)'=\det A\;\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}A')$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $n\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let $$A:I\longrightarrow M_n(\mathbb R),\qquad A(t)=\bigl(a_{ij}(t)\bigr),$$ be a matrix-valued curve whose entries $a_{ij}:I\to\mathbb R$ are differentiable at $t_0\in I$ ([[def-derivative]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]); write $A'(t_0):=\bigl(a_{ij}'(t_0)\bigr)$ ([[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Suppose $A(t)$ is invertible for every $t\in I$ ([[thm-real-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-nonzero]], [[cor-inverse-matrix-by-adjugate]]). Then $t\mapsto\det A(t)$ is differentiable at $t_0$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]) and $$(\det A)'(t_0)=\det A(t_0)\;\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(A(t_0)^{-1}A'(t_0)\bigr),$$ with the trace of [[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]]. In particular, a $C^1$ matrix curve with invertible values has $(\det A)'=\det A\,\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}A')$ on all of $I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

items.title: The transport theorem for a $C^1$ family of diffeomorphisms: $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\psi_t(B)}f=\int_{\psi_t(B)}(\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fw))$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the change-of-variables theorem below. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval ([[def-interval]]), let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region ([[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]) and let $\psi:I\times O\to\mathbb R^3$ be a motion of $B$ on $I$ in the sense of [[def-cm-continuum-motion]], with associated spatial velocity $$w\bigl(t,\psi(t,X)\bigr)=\partial_t\psi(t,X)$$ and Jacobian $J(t,X)=\det D_X\psi_t(X)$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]], [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]]). Let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$, put $$\Sigma:=\bigl\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\psi_t(\overline B)\bigr\},$$ and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ containing $\Sigma$. Then $$F(t):=\int_{\psi_t(B)}f(t,x)\,dx$$ is defined and differentiable on $J_0$ ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]), and for every $t\in J_0$ $$F'(t)=\int_{\psi_t(B)}\bigl(\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fw)\bigr)(t,x)\,dx,$$ with the divergence and spatial derivative of [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]] and the Lebesgue integral of [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]. The same formula holds componentwise for $f$ replaced by a $C^1$ vector field.

items.title: Local mass balance: conservation on every material subregion is equivalent to $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport theorem. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a material region, let $\chi$ be a motion of $B$ on $I$ ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]) with spatial velocity $u$, let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ be an open set containing the swept region $$\Sigma:=\bigl\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\ x\in\chi_t(\overline B)\bigr\}.$$ Let $\rho:U\to(0,\infty)$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); call it a **density field**. A **material subregion** is a nonempty bounded open $B'\subseteq B$ with $\overline{B'}\subseteq B$ ([[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]); for such $B'$ the same $\chi$ is a motion of $B'$. **(i) Localization.** If for every material subregion $B'$ and every $t\in J_0$ $$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho(t,x)\,dx=0, \tag{CM}$$ then $$\partial_t\rho(t,x)+\operatorname{div}\bigl(\rho u\bigr)(t,x)=0$$ for every $(t,x)\in J_0\times\chi_t(B)$, with the material derivative and divergence of [[def-cm-euclidean-spatial-calculus]]. **(ii) Converse.** Conversely, if $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$ on an open neighbourhood of $\Sigma$ in $U$, then (CM) holds for every material subregion $B'$ and every $t\in J_0$.

items.title: A continuous traction field balanced on every piecewise $C^1$ region is given by a continuous stress matrix, and $t(-n)=-t(n)$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ where the surface and divergence machinery of the cited items assumes it. Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $t:O\times S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous, where $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:\|n\|_2=1\}$ is the unit sphere, and let $g:O\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous and bounded, with $C_g:=\sup_{O}\|g\|_2<+\infty$. Suppose that for every bounded piecewise $C^1$ Euclidean domain $D$ with a specified finite presentation ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) whose closure lies in $O$ and whose associated pieces lie in $O$, $$ \int_{\partial D}t\bigl(y,\nu_D(y)\bigr)\,dS(y)+\int_Dg(y)\,dy=0, \tag{B} $$ where $\nu_D$ is the actual outward unit normal off the edge set of the presentation, the boundary term is the sum of the surface integrals over the specified faces ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and values of the normal on the edge set are irrelevant. Then there is a unique continuous map $$\sigma:O\longrightarrow M_3(\mathbb R)$$ with $$t(y,n)=\sigma(y)n\qquad\text{for every }(y,n)\in O\times S^2,$$ the product being matrix-vector multiplication ([[def-matrix-space]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]). Explicitly, the columns of $\sigma(y)$ are the vectors $t(y,e_1),t(y,e_2),t(y,e_3)$; and necessarily $$t(y,-n)=-t(y,n)\qquad\text{for every }(y,n)\in O\times S^2 .$$

items.title: Exact plane-wave solutions of the isotropic linear elastic model, with longitudinal and transverse speeds
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $\rho_0>0$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\mu>0$, let $a,k\in\mathbb R^3$ and $\omega\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, and define the **plane wave** $$\xi:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3,\qquad \xi(t,x):=a\cos\bigl(\langle k,x\rangle_2-\omega t\bigr),$$ with the Euclidean inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_2$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Let $e:=\frac12(D\xi+D\xi^{\mathsf T})$ and $\sigma:=\lambda(\operatorname{tr}e)I_3+2\mu e$ be the strain and stress of the isotropic linear elastic model with parameters $(\lambda,\mu)$ ([[def-cm-linear-elastic-constitutive-law]]). Then the componentwise identity $$\rho_0\,\partial_t^2\xi_i=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j\sigma_{ij}\qquad(i=1,2,3)$$ holds on all of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ if and only if $$\rho_0\omega^2a=\mu|k|_2^2\,a+(\lambda+\mu)\,\langle k,a\rangle_2\,k . \tag{D}$$ Consequently, for $a\ne0$: if $a$ is parallel to $k$ (**longitudinal**), then $\rho_0\omega^2=(\lambda+2\mu)|k|_2^2$; if $a$ is orthogonal to $k$ (**transverse**), then $\rho_0\omega^2=\mu|k|_2^2$. Under the positivity hypothesis $\lambda+\frac{2\mu}{3}>0$ both squared speeds are positive, so both branches have real positive frequencies.

items.title: Sine coefficients, sine series and the odd periodic extension
items.design_state: completed-local-definition; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $L>0$. A function $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is **$L$-periodic** when $F(x+L)=F(x)$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$, and **odd** when $F(-x)=-F(x)$ for all $x$. **(a) Sine coefficients.** Let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and $L$-periodic; then $\int_0^L|F|<\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). For every integer $n\ge1$ the **$n$-th sine coefficient** of $F$ is $$b_n(F):=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^LF(x)\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr)dx \qquad \in\mathbb R ,$$ an ordinary Lebesgue integral of a continuous function on a compact interval ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]). The **sine series** of $F$ is the series of functions $$\sum_{n\ge1}b_n(F)\sin\!\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr),$$ whose $N$-th **partial sum** is $S_N^{\rm s}F(x):=\sum_{n\le N}b_n(F)\sin(n\pi x/L)$. **(b) Odd periodic extension.** Let $F:[0,L]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with $F(0)=F(L)=0$. The **odd $2L$-periodic extension** of $F$ is the function on $\mathbb R$ defined by $$F^{\rm odd}(x):=\begin{cases}F(x),&0\le x\le L,\\ -F(-x),&-L\le x\le 0,\end{cases}\qquad F^{\rm odd}(x+2L):=F^{\rm odd}(x).$$ Equivalently, $F^{\rm odd}$ is the unique $2L$-periodic odd function whose restriction to $[0,L]$ is $F$ (the two definitions agree at $0$ and $L$ because both values vanish; the extension is well defined and continuous). (c) The **fundamental frequency** of mode $n$ is $\omega_n:=cn\pi/L$ for the wave speed $c>0$ fixed by the context.

items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $T,L>0$ and $R:=[0,T]\times[0,L]$ ([[def-interval]]). For each $k\in\mathbb N$ let $u_k$ be of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Suppose that on $R$: $$u_k\to u,\quad \partial_tu_k\to v,\quad \partial_xu_k\to w,\quad \partial_t^2u_k\to v_2,\quad \partial_t\partial_xu_k\to z,\quad \partial_x^2u_k\to w_2$$ pointwise for $u$ and uniformly for the five derivative sequences ([[def-continuity-real]]). Then $u$ is $C^2$ on the interior of $R$, all listed limits are continuous on $R$, and on the interior $$\partial_tu=v,\quad \partial_xu=w,\quad \partial_t^2u=v_2,\quad \partial_t\partial_xu=\partial_x\partial_tu=z,\quad \partial_x^2u=w_2 ,$$ the derivatives extending continuously to $R$.

items.title: Repeated integration by parts gives $|b_n(F)|\le 2L^5M_5/(\pi^5n^5)$ for odd $2L$-periodic $C^5$ functions and $|b_n(G)|\le 2L^4M_4/(\pi^4n^4)$ for $C^4$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $L>0$. Let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^5$ and let $G:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^4$ ([[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); put $$M_5:=\sup_{\mathbb R}|F^{(5)}|<+\infty,\qquad M_4:=\sup_{\mathbb R}|G^{(4)}|<+\infty .$$ Then for every integer $n\ge1$, with the sine coefficients $b_n$ of [[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]], $$|b_n(F)|\le\frac{2L^5M_5}{\pi^5n^5},\qquad |b_n(G)|\le\frac{2L^4M_4}{\pi^4n^4}.$$

items.title: The smooth fixed-end string: the sine series solves the wave equation with the given data, uniquely, with an explicit tail bound
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $L>0$, $c>0$. Let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^5$ and let $G:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be odd and $2L$-periodic of class $C^4$ ([[def-cm-sine-coefficients-of-periodic-functions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), with $M_5:=\sup|F^{(5)}|<\infty$, $M_4:=\sup|G^{(4)}|<\infty$. Put $$a_n:=b_n(F),\qquad d_n:=\frac{b_n(G)}{\omega_n},\qquad \omega_n:=\frac{cn\pi}{L}\qquad(n\ge1),$$ and define, for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R^2$, $$u(t,x):=\sum_{n\ge1}\Bigl[a_n\cos(\omega_nt)+d_n\sin(\omega_nt)\Bigr]\sin\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr). \tag{S}$$ Then: **(i)** the series (S) and the termwise series of $\partial_tu,\partial_xu,\partial_t^2u,\partial_t\partial_xu,\partial_x^2u$ converge absolutely and uniformly on every strip $[-T,T]\times[0,L]$; the sum $u$ is $C^2$, is odd and $2L$-periodic in $x$, satisfies $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$, obeys the fixed-end conditions $u(t,0)=u(t,L)=0$, and has $$u(0,x)=F(x),\qquad u_t(0,x)=G(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R).$$ **(ii)** (Uniqueness.) If $v$ is $C^2$ on $[0,T]\times[0,L]$ for some $T>0$, satisfies $v_{tt}=c^2v_{xx}$ there, $v(t,0)=v(t,L)=0$ for all $t$, and $v(0,\cdot)=v_t(0,\cdot)=0$, then $v=0$ on $[0,T]\times[0,L]$. **(iii)** (Tail bound.) For every $N\ge1$ and every $(t,x)\in[-T,T]\times[0,L]$, $$\Bigl|u(t,x)-\sum_{n\le N}\Bigl[a_n\cos(\omega_nt)+d_n\sin(\omega_nt)\Bigr]\sin\Bigl(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\Bigr)\Bigr|\le C\,(N+1)^{-4},$$ where $C:=2\bigl(\frac{2L^5M_5}{\pi^5}+\frac{2L^5M_4}{c\pi^5}\bigr)$.

references.title: R. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (arXiv:0903.3845), Chapters 1–2 (Fourier coefficients, summability and the uniqueness theorem (2.14))
K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 6.5 (standing waves of the fixed-end string)

items.title: Transport of a translating rigid region: the rate integral vanishes for a travelling profile
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $B:=B_1(0)\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open unit ball ([[def-metric-ball]]), a nonempty bounded open set and hence a material region in the sense of [[def-cm-material-region-and-density]]; let $v\in\mathbb R^3$ be fixed, and let $$\psi(t,X):=X+tv\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ X\in\mathbb R^3)$$ be the uniform translation motion of [[def-cm-continuum-motion]] (each $\psi_t$ is the identity plus a translation, a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism with $D_X\psi_t=I_3$). Let $h:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and define the travelling profile $$f(t,x):=h(x-tv)\qquad\bigl((t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\bigr).$$ Then $\int_{\psi_t(B)}f(t,x)\,dx$ is independent of $t$, while the transport integrand vanishes pointwise: $$\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fv)=0,$$ so the transport theorem reproduces the constant rate $0$.

items.statement: Take $\lambda=2$, $\mu=1$, $\rho_0=1$ ([[def-cm-linear-elastic-constitutive-law]]: here $\lambda+\frac{2\mu}{3}=\frac83>0$). Let $k=(\pi,0,0)$, $a=(1,0,0)$ and $$\xi(t,x)=a\cos(\pi x_1-\omega t),\qquad \omega:=2\pi .$$ Then $\xi$ is a longitudinal plane wave with speed $\sqrt{(\lambda+2\mu)/\rho_0}=2$, and the associated strain and stress satisfy the elastic momentum identity; the strain energy density at time $t$ equals both $W(e)=2\pi^2\sin^2(\pi x_1-\omega t)$ and the decomposition $\mu|e_0|_F^2+(\lambda/2+\mu/3)(\operatorname{tr}e)^2$ with the same value.

items.title: The first sine mode with matched velocity data: exact solution and the numerical tail bound $8(N+1)^{-4}$
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Let $L>0$, $c>0$ and define the odd $2L$-periodic $C^\infty$ datum $$F(x):=\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad G(x):=\frac{c\pi}{L}\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi x}{L}\Bigr).$$ Then the sine coefficients of [the definition] are $b_1(F)=1$ and $b_n(F)=0$ for $n\ge2$, and $b_1(G)=c\pi/L$, $b_n(G)=0$ for $n\ge2$; the series solution of the string theorem is the finite expression $$u(t,x)=\bigl[\cos(\omega_1t)+\sin(\omega_1t)\bigr]\sin\Bigl(\frac{\pi x}{L}\Bigr),\qquad \omega_1=\frac{c\pi}{L},$$ which solves $u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}$ with $u(0,\cdot)=F$, $u_t(0,\cdot)=G$ and $u(t,0)=u(t,L)=0$; its tail beyond the first mode vanishes, and the numerical bound of the string theorem at these data is $$|u(t,x)-u_1(t,x)|\le 8\,(N+1)^{-4}\qquad(N\ge2),$$ so the general bound is valid but far from sharp on this datum.

items.title: Riemann data $u_L=3$, $u_R=1$: shock speed and entropy coefficients, and a rarefaction check
items.reference: batch-8 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: Take $u_L=3>u_R=1$ in the shock of [[thm-cm-burgers-riemann-shock-and-rarefaction]]. The shock speed is $s=\frac{u_L+u_R}{2}=2$. For the entropy pair $(\eta_k,q_k)$: - for $k=2$, which lies strictly between $u_R=1$ and $u_L=3$, the interface coefficient is $s[\eta_2]-[q_2]=1$; - for $k=0$, which lies outside the interval $[1,3]$, the coefficient is $s[\eta_0]-[q_0]=0$; both nonnegative, in accordance with the theorem's closed formula $s[\eta_k]-[q_k]=-(k-u_L)(k-u_R)$ in the interior case and $=0$ in the exterior case. For the rarefaction with $u_L=1<u_R=3$, the fan $u=x/t$ satisfies $u_t+uu_x=0$ identically, and the entropy residuals vanish because the fan is continuous.

items.title: A four-node cyclic chain mode with $a=c=1$: exact ODE check, dispersion value $\omega^2=2$, and the continuum error bound

items.statement: Take $N=4$, $a=1$, $c=1$ in the cyclic chain of [[def-cm-cyclic-spring-chain]]. The wave number $\kappa=\pi/2$ gives $$\omega^2=\frac{4c^2}{a^2}\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\kappa a}{2}\Bigr)=4\sin^2\Bigl(\frac{\pi}{4}\Bigr)=2,\qquad \omega=\sqrt2,$$ and the profile $q_j(t)=\cos\bigl(\frac{\pi j}{2}-\sqrt2\,t\bigr)$, $j\in\mathbb Z/4$, solves the chain equation exactly; the continuum comparison at this wave number gives the exact error $|\omega^2-c^2\kappa^2|=\frac{\pi^2}{4}-2$ against the exact bound $\frac{c^2\kappa^4a^2}{12}=\frac{\pi^4}{192}$.
